I think the one complicating issue here in turning against publishers entirely is that that publishers, at least today, are not necessarily about access to the papers themselves. Even without this site if you want a paper there's a good chance if you email one of the authors, he'll send you a copy for free. What the journals provide, and the more reputable the journal the more this effect is in play, is a filtering and review system letting you know that what you're reading has been reviewed, approved, and found relevant by other experts in the field.

There are definitely ways to decentralize this and take publishers out of the picture, but I think just damning publishers without having an alternative solution in place that provides the same benefits would be foolhardy.
